treatment: Tamoxifen vs breast RT vs breast RT + tamoxifen
population: 1,009 women with node-negative invasive breast cancer ≤1 cm after lumpectomy
relativeEffect: RT+tamoxifen vs tamoxifen: large reduction in IBTR
benefitText: IBTR was 2.8% with RT + tamoxifen versus 16.5% with tamoxifen alone.
harmText: No single dominant fixed-time toxicity endpoint supports a defensible NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: Tamoxifen did not substitute for breast RT; combined therapy gave the lowest local recurrence.
clinicalQuestion: After lumpectomy for node-negative invasive breast cancer ≤1 cm, can tamoxifen substitute for breast RT?
refs: NSABP B-21 trial report and NSABP review

treatment: 18 months ADT + RT vs 6 months ADT + RT
population: 1,071 men with locally advanced prostate cancer
benefitText: Ten-year adjusted prostate-cancer-specific mortality was 9.7% vs 13.3%.
harmText: The main trade-off is longer ADT exposure; a single fixed-time severe-toxicity endpoint was not appropriate for NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: Extending ADT from 6 to 18 months produced a modest absolute reduction in prostate-cancer-specific mortality.
clinicalQuestion: Does extending ADT from 6 to 18 months improve long-term outcomes with RT?
refs: Denham JW, et al. Lancet Oncol. 2019;20:267–281.

treatment: ADT + RT + docetaxel vs ADT + RT
population: 563 eligible patients; high-risk localized prostate cancer
benefitText: Ten-year OS was 69% vs 64%, but the long-term analysis did not show a statistically significant difference.
harmText: Two grade 5 events occurred in the docetaxel arm and none in control in the long-term report.
clinicalInterpretation: The initial docetaxel signal did not translate into a definitive long-term survival benefit.
clinicalQuestion: Does adding adjuvant docetaxel to ADT + RT improve survival?

treatment: Adjuvant RT + 6 months triptorelin vs early salvage RT + 6 months triptorelin
population: 424 men with adverse pathology and positive margins after prostatectomy
benefitText: Five-year EFS was 92% vs 90%; the trial was underpowered because of unexpectedly low event rates.
harmText: Late grade ≥2 GU toxicity was 59% vs 22%, an absolute increase of 37 points.
clinicalInterpretation: Routine adjuvant RT did not improve EFS over early salvage in this modern strategy and caused more late toxicity.
clinicalQuestion: Is immediate adjuvant RT superior to early salvage RT after prostatectomy?
refs: Tilki D, et al. Lancet Oncol. 2020;21:1341–1352.

population: 821 patients with previously treated advanced clear-cell RCC
benefitText: Median OS was 25.0 vs 19.6 months; ORR was 25% vs 5% (+20 points, NNT≈5 for response).
clinicalInterpretation: Nivolumab improved OS despite little difference in median PFS.
clinicalQuestion: Does nivolumab improve survival versus everolimus?
refs: Motzer RJ, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:1803–1813.

population: 723 patients with metastatic RCC after prior systemic therapy
benefitText: Median PFS was 6.7 vs 4.7 months; ORR was 19.4% vs 9.4%, +10 points.
clinicalInterpretation: Axitinib improved PFS and response over sorafenib without a demonstrated OS advantage.
clinicalQuestion: Does axitinib improve disease control versus sorafenib?

treatment: Neoadjuvant paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin followed by surgery
population: 30 men with cN2–cN3 penile SCC without distant metastases
benefitText: 15/30 (50%) had objective response; 22/30 underwent surgery; 3/30 achieved pathologic complete response.
harmText: Grade 3–4 anemia, neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and neuropathy were each reported in <5%.
clinicalInterpretation: TIP provided a clinically meaningful response benchmark for bulky regional penile cancer, but causal treatment effects cannot be estimated.
clinicalQuestion: Can neoadjuvant TIP enable consolidative surgery in bulky regional penile cancer?
refs: Pagliaro LC, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2010;28:3851–3857.

treatment: 6-week BCG induction vs induction + one BCG instillation every 3 months for 3 years
benefitText: Five-year relapse was 38.5% with maintenance versus 33.5% with induction alone.
harmText: 20 patients stopped maintenance for toxicity versus 5 in the induction-only group.
clinicalInterpretation: This three-monthly maintenance schedule did not reduce recurrence or progression compared with induction alone.
clinicalQuestion: Does three-monthly BCG maintenance for 3 years improve outcomes after induction?
refs: Martínez-Piñeiro L, et al. Eur Urol. 2015;68:256–262.

treatment: MRI vs CT; 3 scans vs 7 scans
population: Stage I seminoma after orchiectomy managed with surveillance
benefitText: Stage ≥IIC relapse was 0.6% with MRI vs 2.6% with CT. Three scans produced 2.8% vs 0.3% with seven scans, a +2.5-point increase that remained within the 5.7-point noninferiority margin.
harmText: Three scans increased stage ≥IIC relapse by 2.5 percentage points versus seven scans at 6 years.
clinicalInterpretation: MRI was noninferior to CT, and a reduced three-scan schedule stayed within the prespecified advanced-relapse margin.
clinicalQuestion: Can MRI replace CT and surveillance be reduced from seven to three scans?
refs: Joffe JK, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2022.

population: 89 patients with poor-prognosis metastatic germ-cell tumours
benefitText: Favourable response was 74.4% vs 60.9%, an absolute increase of 13.5 points.
harmText: Grade ≥3 toxicity was 96% vs 63%, an absolute increase of 33 points.
clinicalInterpretation: Intensification improved response but produced major toxicity and was not powered as a definitive phase III survival comparison.
clinicalQuestion: Does intensified CBOP/BEP improve favourable response in poor-prognosis GCT?
refs: Huddart RA, et al. Eur Urol. 2015;67:534–543.
